recognize_zh: 高倍血片中紅血球呈兩群：一群淡染、只剩細邊的低色素細胞，另一群是中央有血紅素點的標靶細胞（target cells），並夾雜淚滴狀碎片，符合地中海型貧血的紅血球變化。
features: Dimorphic red cell population: markedly hypochromic, thin-rimmed 'ghost-like' cells alongside better-hemoglobinized cells
Numerous target cells with a central dot of hemoglobin (bull's-eye appearance)
Red cells small relative to expected normocytes (microcytosis), with anisocytosis
Poikilocytes including a small teardrop-shaped fragment
Occasional platelet in background; no nucleated cells in this field
describe_en: High-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows a dimorphic red cell population composed of markedly hypochromic microcytes with only a thin rim of hemoglobin and better-hemoglobinized cells, many of which are target cells. Anisopoikilocytosis is present, including a small teardrop-shaped fragment. No nucleated red cells or red cell inclusions are identified in this field. Findings are consistent with thalassemia; the dimorphic pattern may reflect prior transfusion.

ddx.vs: Iron deficiency shows pencil cells and hypochromia with fewer target cells and a disproportionately low MCV-to-RBC count relationship, and iron studies are low rather than normal or high.
HbC produces abundant target cells but they are well hemoglobinized, often with rhomboid HbC crystals, and hemoglobin electrophoresis shows HbC.
Sideroblastic anemia also gives a dimorphic hypochromic population but shows Pappenheimer bodies and ring sideroblasts on marrow iron stain.
Liver disease target cells are normochromic and often macrocytic, without the hypochromic microcytic population.
